blocks.html: Welcome friend. Today is the perfect day to learn how to live code!

Hopefully you’re as excited to get started coding your own sounds as I am to show you. It’s going to be a really fun ride where you’ll learn all about music, synthesis, programming, composition, performance and more.

But wait, how rude of me! Let me introduce myself - I’m Sam Aaron the creator of Sonic Pi. I initially designed Sonic Pi as an introductory teaching tool for Computer Science in schools. However, whilst it’s still great at that it has also evolved into a powerful musical instrument that will let you express yourself in new ways.

I believe that expressing yourself with code is the best way to learn how to code. Sonic Pi was designed with this in mind at all times, so be prepared to experiment, play and let the music that’s in your heart out through the code.
Watching others live code is a really great way to learn. I regularly stream live on https://youtube.com/samaaron so please do drop by, say hi and ask me lots of questions :-)

This tutorial is divided up into sections grouped by category. Whilst I’ve written it to have an easy learning progression from start to finish, feel very free just to dip in and out of sections as you see fit. If you feel that there’s something missing, do let me know and I’ll consider it for a future version.
Also, if you have any thoughts, or ideas for improving Sonic Pi itself - please pass them on - feedback is so helpful. You never know, your idea might be the next big feature!
